verdicts.misleading_risk: The inheritance risk is real, but the generator part would make the form write authors, license and DOI that live in labconstrictor-app.yaml, so one fact would sit in two files. The draft's facts check out: five authors and ORCIDs match the Zenodo record 20758747, the arXiv title and authors match, and 19074199 is the concept DOI. The 'Hidalgo-Cenalmor' spelling is the one arXiv and Crossref use; Zenodo has 'Hidalgo Cenalmor'. Guarding only the Streamlit form is incomplete. A repo made with 'Use this template' and no form would still inherit the file, as it inherits the README today.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Out of scope for the site work; do not build it now. The template README already carries the preprint citation and the Zenodo badge, and the site does not read a template CITATION.cff. If the authors want GitHub's 'Cite this repository' box on the template, do two small things in this order. First, in LabConstrictor_streamlit/app.py, next to the README move (about line 660), delete a root CITATION.cff whose title is 'LabConstrictor'. Second, add the draft CFF to the template with the arXiv paper as preferred-citation and the concept DOI at top level. Drop the per-app CFF generator in manifest_form.py. Never add a .zenodo.json to the template. The authors must decide the spelling 'Hidalgo-Cenalmor' versus 'Hidalgo Cenalmor'.
verdicts.evidence: Checked LabConstrictor on disk and on GitHub raw: neither CITATION.cff nor .zenodo.json exists. LabConstrictor_streamlit/app.py lines 658-690 move only README.md. Zenodo API: record 20758747 is version 0.0.2 (2026-06-19); the concept record is 19074199; the doi.org link for 19074199 redirects to 20758747. Zenodo's creators for 20758747 carry the same five ORCIDs as the draft. arXiv API: the 2603.10704 title and 5 authors match. The record's related identifier is arXiv:2603.10704 with relation 'describes'. The template's README line 2 has the badge for 20758747 and lines 66-69 give the preprint as the citation. The sync migrations are scripts per version; I did not read them all, so 'sync never manages root files' is only partly verified.

verdicts.misleading_risk: Two drafted facts are unsafe. (1) The NucleiSky draft splits 'Johannes Kumra Ahnlide' as family 'Kumra Ahnlide'. Crossref for 10.1242/jcs.265152 gives given 'Johannes Kumra' and family 'Ahnlide', and the Zenodo data record and the README BibTeX agree; the draft's split would print a wrong name in GitHub's citation. (2) The draft sets the software authors equal to the paper authors with no source, but a top-level CFF author list is a claim about who wrote the software. For the VLab4Mic wrapper, git log shows Saraiva, Henriques and one other committer, not the 8 paper authors. The VLab4Mic software lives in HenriquesLab/VLab4Mic, which has no CFF either. A CFF in the wrapper repo may also point GitHub's box at a repo that is only the installer distribution.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Keep it as owner-side work in the app repositories, done by their owners; the site does not depend on it. Use the paper authors only if each owner confirms it; the top-level 'authors' field is required, so they must name someone. Fix the NucleiSky split: family 'Ahnlide', given 'Johannes Kumra'. Do the two CellMigrationLab repos first. NucleiSky: concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21071484, JCS article 10.1242/jcs.265152, month 8, year 2026. CellTracksColab: PLOS Biology 22(8), 2024, 10.1371/journal.pbio.3002740, no top-level doi because no software record was found. For VLab4Mic, ask the owners whether the CFF goes in the upstream HenriquesLab/VLab4Mic or in the wrapper; the paper authors and DOI are verified (Crossref and bioRxiv, Damián Martínez with ORCID, first author), but the software authorship is not. Where a README already gives the same citation, link the README to the CFF rather than keeping two copies.
verdicts.evidence: Raw GitHub requests return 404 for CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json in NucleiSky, CellTracksColab, LabConstrictor-VLab4Mic and HenriquesLab/VLab4Mic. Crossref confirms the JCS paper (8 authors; issued 2026-08-14), the PLOS Biology paper (7 authors, volume 22, issue 8, 2024-08-08) and the bioRxiv paper (8 authors, 2026-06-04). The bioRxiv API shows 'Martinez, D.' and Crossref shows 'Damián Martínez', which agrees with the README. GitHub docs confirm that 'preferred-citation' makes the box cite the article. The VLab4Mic README lines 58-72 hold the BibTeX; the repo is HenriquesLab/LabConstrictor-VLab4Mic.

verdicts.misleading_risk: A .zenodo.json would be a second copy of the creators next to the CFF from G2, and Zenodo reads only .zenodo.json once it exists, so the two could drift apart. The draft also repeats the 'Kumra Ahnlide' name split that Crossref contradicts, and the license id 'MIT' is unverified against Zenodo's vocabulary (the API shows 'mit-license'). ORCIDs for the three Zenodo-data-record authors (Hidalgo-Cenalmor, Henriques, Del Rosario, Jacquemet) are verified from the data record 20721416; the other four authors have none, and none should be invented. Which CFF fields Zenodo maps (creators, license, related identifiers) is not confirmed: the Zenodo help page says CITATION.cff is supported but does not list the fields. The 'isDescribedBy' relation cannot come from a CFF.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Do not add a .zenodo.json. Treat this as part of the NucleiSky CFF in G2: Zenodo supports CITATION.cff for GitHub releases and uses it as long as no .zenodo.json is present, so the CFF fixes the creators ('Iván Hidalgo', 'guijacquemet') on the next release with one source of truth. After the next release, check the new record's creators on zenodo.org. Whoever owns record 21238020 should edit its existing creators and add the JCS paper as a related identifier by hand; the old 0.1.1 record cannot be changed by a file. The 'describes' versus 'isDescribedBy' relation on template record 20758747 is the authors' call, not a site task.
verdicts.evidence: Zenodo API for 21238020 (0.1.1, 2026-07-07): creators are 'Iván Hidalgo' and 'guijacquemet', no ORCIDs, one related identifier (the GitHub tag URL, isSupplementTo), license mit-license. doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21071484 redirects to record 21238020. Zenodo's help page says that with both files present only .zenodo.json is used and CITATION.cff is ignored. The 20758747 record has related identifier arXiv:2603.10704 with relation 'describes'.

verdicts.misleading_risk: Fetching, schema-checking and rendering each app's CITATION.cff is too much for 3 apps with a DOI. It would put the DOI in both the manifest and the CFF, a new 'written twice' case that the manifest `doi` already covers. It needs a new parser, a CFF schema and a failure mode on every build, and it depends on G2 shipping in repos the site team does not own. The 'No publication listed' line would state an absence the site cannot verify; for the Demo, Playground and Guess the Condition apps it would be noise or wrong. Moving the DOIs from main.html into data/site.yaml does not work as written: main.html is the theme template and reads only mkdocs config, not data/site.yaml.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Three small changes. (1) Footer: replace the single 'Cite LabConstrictor' link (hard-coded to version record 20758747, 0.0.2) with 'Cite the paper' (https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2603.10704, the preprint the template README recommends) and 'Cite the software archive' (the concept DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19074199, which today redirects to the latest version). Keep the two addresses in one place: mkdocs.yml `extra.citation`, read by main.html through config.extra, and delete the unused `citation_doi` from data/site.yaml. Only the authors know which link they want to be the main one; the README names the preprint. (2) Apps: no CFF parsing. The manifest `doi` already renders as the Cite row for NucleiSky and CellTracksColab. Add `doi: 10.64898/2026.06.02.729521` to VLab4Mic's manifest (it matches the schema pattern and is the preprint its README recommends), and change the schema description at line 36 from 'paper or archive' to 'the paper to cite'. Everything else stays where it is. (3) Do not copy the reference text into the site; later, if wanted, show title and authors by looking up the DOI at fetch time, only after the authors ask for it. If the Cite row is moved nearer 'Using it', add the pattern to DESIGN.md first, which has no citation entry. Add tests for the footer links and the Cite row, including the failure case when extra.citation is missing.
verdicts.evidence: overrides/main.html line 100 hard-codes https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20758747. data/site.yaml line 15 `citation_doi` has the same URL, and a search of scripts, overrides and tests finds no reader of it. The preprint DOI appears only in planning notes, nowhere on the built site. pages_apps.py lines 152-153 render the Cite row only when `doi` is present; the snapshot has a doi for CellTracksColab (10.1371/journal.pbio.3002740) and NucleiSky (10.1242/jcs.265152), and none for VLab4Mic, Playground, Demo and GuessTheCondition. seed/manifests/LabConstrictor-VLab4Mic.yaml has no doi. Neither mkdocs.yml nor the generators read a mkdocs `extra` citation today; `extra.listed` is the only entry. AGENTS.md sections 'Sources of truth', 'Untrusted input' and 'No silent fallbacks' were read. pages_apps.py is 208 lines, so one more row fits without a new module; the auditor's claim that a new module is needed holds only for the CFF-parsing design.
